findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs to be stored above green beans and milk in the upright kitchen cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were relocated to the bottom shelf. Ensure all animal products are stored below ready-to-eat foods in the cooler to prevent cross contamination. A handout was provided by the inspector to staff for future reference.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ventilation covers and shelves above the triple sink and hand sink to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure staff are cleaning these surfaces frequently to prevent cross contamination with food containers and clean dishes. Ensure these surfaces are clean prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed bag of fabric on basin of hand washing sink in kitchen. Bag was removed during inspection. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on block of American cheese slices. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. The cheese arrived in January and was put into use. Cheese was discarded. Freeze sections of cheese and use as needed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Walls in the kitchen area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11. The wall next to the light switch is in disrepair. Also, the area around the pipe at the counter level is not sealed. Seal around pipe and repair the wall.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food surfaces are soiled with crumbs and dust 1) top of white drawers 2) shelves of both cooling units 3) the drain board. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored in a caddy that is soiled with dust and crumbs. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. Also, observed clean drinking cups to be stored in contact with an absorbent towel in a strainer.  All non food surfaces shall be smooth non absorbent and easily cleansable. Do not drain on towels or absorbent surfaces. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The shelves in the kitchen cooler have some soil. Clean and maintain free of soil accumulation. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Upon entry, a jacket we observed on the kitchen counter. No food prep is taking place at the time. Provide enough adequate storage for employee belongings. Jacket we moved. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment: Observed shell eggs in the facility. The eggs are not pasteurized. 750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.  As a facility that serves a highly susceptible population shell eggs cooked for service must be pasteurized.  The shell eggs currently in the facility will not be cooked for service but may be used in cakes and cookies.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Employee is using cloths to dry dishes and remove water spots. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Allow food contact surfaces to air day and avoid potential contamination by drying with a cloth or towel of any kind.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: Employee is washing hands in the 3 part sink. 750-1120c Sinks used for food preparation or for washing equipment or utensils shall not be used for hand washing. Wash hands in the hand sink provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Vents in the facility kitchen are soiled with dust and have large openings. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean the vents,

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: Observed a canister of Clorox wipes to be stored on the shelf above the prep area mingled with food. 750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals. Canister was removed to area with other chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: There is no certified food manager employed by the facility currently. 750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Metal storage cabinet has stuck/painted on sugar/debris in the bottom. Maintenance worker tried sanding and spray painting to fix the issue. The bottom inside the cabinet is still not smooth or easily cleanable. Staff showed inspector an invoice for a new 24 gauge steel standard storage cabinet that has been ordered to replace the current cabinet.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
750.1120d - Work was done to adjust/repair the automatic faucet at the kitchen handsink, but the faucet was once again observed to be running for less than 15 seconds. Water only ran for about 9 to 12 seconds (stopwatch on iPhone used to verify). 
If the automatic faucet cannot be repaired to run for at least 15 seconds, then replace it with a manual faucet. 

All self-closing, slow closing, or metering faucet used shall be designed to provide a flow of water for at least 15 seconds without the need to reactivate the faucet.

B) Effort was made to cut the spray foam flush with the wall and paint around water lines and plumbing in the kitchen below 3 part sink drain board. Some of the spray foam still needs to be painted (around water lines). Finish painting the spray foam.

All walls, ceilings, and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 & 250 - A) Cooked chicken in the bottom of the kitchen fridge had surface and internal temperatures of 48F and 46F respectively. Staff noted the chicken was out earlier for lunch prep but was placed back in the fridge immediately after use. The chicken was moved to the storage fridge, which was observed holding foods consistently at temperatures below 41F.
B) Almond milk. 1% milk, and lactose free 2% milk in the kitchen fridge had surface temperatures of 56F-60F. Internal temperatures for the lactose free milk and 1% milk were observed at 59F and 56F. All of the milks in question were out during lunch service. Director stated ice packs are used to surround milk in bowls to try and keep products cold. The ice packs were not successful at keeping milks cold today. All milks were discarded during the inspection. The use of time control for smaller portions of milk was discussed.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - A) Cooked chicken in the kitchen fridge did not have a date mark on it. Director noted it was prepared on Tuesday of this week. Benefit of the doubt was given; product was dated and kept for use.
B) American cheese slices in a ziploc bag in the kitchen fridge had a date mark of 9/20. Cheese slices were discarded in the trash.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous, ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store raw foods below and away from ready to eat foods.

750.830g - Chlorine test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions. Obtain and use chlorine test strips to verify bleach solutions are at proper sanitizing concentrations.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - An accumulation of food crumbs was observed inside the bottom utensil storage drawer of counter top organizer. Maintain storage areas for cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment clean to protect items from potential contamination.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text:
750.600 - Plastic yogurt containers were being re-used for the storage of ketchup and grape jelly. Obtain and use proper re-usable containers for food storage.

Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Packaging and containers that came with other food items in them may not be re-used for the storage of other foods and should not be kept for food storage purposes once the original food items is gone. Items such as aluminum pans, bread bags, yogurt and sour cream containers, etc. may not be re-used for the storage of other food items. Do not re-use single service items.

All self-closing, slow closing, or metering faucet used shall be designed to provide a flow of water for at least 15 seconds without the need to reactivate the faucet.
